subject: Discovery Recap & Integration/PoC Plan - FastRetail
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery Recap & Integration/PoC Plan - FastRetail

Alex / Sophie -

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed integration / PoC plan so we can align next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I'll update.

Summary of pain points
- Search relevance for product detail pages is inconsistent across regions (notably EU catalog).
- Current in-house ranking stack struggles with latency under peak traffic (300-500 QPS).
- Embeddings pipeline is brittle: long update cycles and no prefix caching, leading to high per-query cost and stale results.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Frontend: React micro-frontends
- Backend: Scala microservices on AWS ECS Fargate
- Vector store: Pinecone (single region), nightly batch updates
- Auth/SSO: Okta + SAML

Success criteria for the PoC
- Match or improve top-3 click-through rate by >= 5% vs current production model.
- Maintain 95th percentile latency <= 120ms under a 200 QPS sustained load in the PoC environment.
- Demonstrate integration with existing Pinecone/embeddings pipeline and a rollout plan for prefix/KV caching.

Proposed integration & onboarding plan (high-level)
- SDKs: Primary PoC work in Python (data eng team) and a Java/Scala client for the backend services. We'll provide both.
- API compatibility: Redwood REST API + code samples for streaming responses. No schema changes required on your side for embeddings calls.
- Milestones / timeline (4-week PoC):
  * Week 0 (this week): Kickoff & environment access (AWS account/VPC peering options, Okta test app). Owners: Ben (Redwood) / Alex (FastRetail).
  * Week 1: Integration of SDK, initial inference calls, and embedding sync test. Owners: Vanessa (SE) / FastRetail data eng.
  * Week 2: Load testing (up to 200 QPS), latency tuning, and prefix cache validation. Owners: Redwood infra + FastRetail backend.
  * Week 3: Quality evaluation vs production metrics, tweak ranking model variant.
  * Week 4: PoC wrap, outcomes, and decision meeting (go/no-go + rollout timeline).

Owners / contacts
- Redwood: Ben Carter (Account Exec) - ben.carter@redwood.com
- Redwood SE: Vanessa Ortiz - vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole - marissa.cole@redwood.com
- FastRetail: Alex Johnson (Prod) - alex.johnson@fastretail.com; Sophie Martinez (Data Eng) - sophie.martinez@fastretail.com

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Alex/Sophie: share a short-lived AWS role or staging credentials (read-only) + Okta test config by EOD Friday so we can provision a PoC environment.
2) Redwood: we'll send a PoC plan & security questionnaire (attached) and a preliminary capacity estimate for the 200 QPS scenario.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff next week (proposed slots Tue/Wed morning PT).

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (PoC plan), fastretail-security-questions.xlsx (security questionnaire)

Thanks - I'll follow up with calendar invites once I get your preferred kickoff slot.

-
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147
redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sophie Martinez <sophie.martinez@fastretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Integration/PoC Plan - FastRetail

Thanks for the clear recap, Ben - this looks right to me. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Data residency: EU catalog data must remain in eu-central-1 for the evaluation dataset. Can Redwood support region-specific inference?
- SSO / provisioning: we can create an Okta test app and a cross-account role. I'll get that to you by Thursday.
- QPS expectations: the 200 QPS sustained is accurate for the initial PoC, but we'd like a short spike test to 500 QPS to understand burst behavior.

We'll loop in our Security team once we get the questionnaire. Sophie, can you confirm if the data extracts will be JSONL? That's our preferred format.

If Redwood can confirm EU-region inference and the spike test, we're good to kick off next week - Tue morning PT works for me.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product - Search | FastRetail
alex.johnson@fastretail.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Integration/PoC Plan - FastRetail

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex. Short answers: yes on both counts.

- EU-region inference: supported. We can provision a PoC instance in eu-central-1 and route EU catalog traffic there for the test. We'll document network requirements for VPC peering.
- Burst testing: we'll include a 500 QPS 5-minute spike in the load test plan and report tail-latencies.

Next actions I'll take today:
- Share updated PoC plan with EU-region notes and a preliminary capacity estimate (will attach before EOD).
- Send a calendar invite for Tue 2026-09-22 09:30 PT for the technical kickoff (please accept / propose alternate if needed).

Marissa / Vanessa - can you please coordinate a short SE/infra pairing session after kickoff to validate SDK usage (Python + Java client)?

Thanks - looking forward to getting started.

-
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
